findings.title: Working-hours check rejects every slot for hosts with more than one availability block on a day
findings.body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns true as soon as ANY block that includes the day has the slot outside its range, and that `true` makes the function return `false`. A host whose schedule has two blocks on one day (e.g. 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00) has two `WorkingHours` entries for that day (see `getWorkingHours` in packages/lib/availability.ts:76-100, which pushes one entry per availability row). A 10:00 slot is outside the 13:00–17:00 block, so it is dropped, and a 14:00 slot is outside the 09:00–12:00 block, so it is dropped as well. Every slot on such days disappears for fixed hosts (and for loose hosts via the 513-518 path), because both call sites now spread `...schedule`, which includes `workingHours` (lines 488-493, 513-518). Before this change `workingHours` was never read here. The check should pass when the slot is inside at least one block for that day, not fail when it is outside one.

The `end` variable on line 142 is also identical to `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` can never differ from the start comparison. A slot that starts inside the block but runs past its end is not rejected. It was probably meant to use `slotEndTime`.

No test covers either case: the only fixtures use a single block per day.

findings.title: Shifted override times wrap past midnight and are silently dropped or placed on the wrong day
findings.body:
`startTime`/`endTime` are now computed as `.add(offset,'minute').hour()*60 + .minute()`. The `hour()` call wraps modulo 24h, with no clamping like `getWorkingHours` does (packages/lib/availability.ts:87-111). If `offset` (invitee offset minus organizer offset) pushes the override over midnight, the start is on one day and the end is on the next. For example, a 09:00–17:00 override with an 18h offset gives start 03:00 and end 11:00, and with a 10h offset gives start 19:00 and end 03:00. In the second case `end < start`, so `buildSlots` skips it (`if (start >= end) continue`, line 68). The user's regular working hours were already removed at lines 228-243, so that day shows no slots and nothing reports an error.

The override is also selected as `activeOverrides` (line 206) by its unshifted instant against the invitee's day, while the minutes are computed after shifting, so the two disagree for large offsets. The shifted time should be clamped or split across days, as `getWorkingHours` does.

findings.title: Dead comparison and UTC-day matching in the date-override check
findings.body:
Line 114 compares two `Dayjs` objects with `===`. That is reference equality and is always false, so the branch never runs. If a zero-length override was meant to block the day, use `.isSame()` or compare `valueOf()`.

The override is matched to a slot by the UTC calendar day of the shifted override start (110-111). For an organizer far from UTC (e.g. UTC+10, 09:00–17:00 local = 23:00–07:00 UTC) the override range spans two UTC days. Slots on the later UTC day do not match, so `dateOverrideExist` stays false for them and they are judged by the normal working-hours block instead of the override. Compare against the override's [start,end) instant range rather than a calendar-day string.

findings.title: Redundant parsing and repeated computation in override mapping
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` goes through `Date.toString()`, which drops milliseconds and relies on string parsing. Use `dayjs(override.start)` or `dayjs.utc(override.start)`. `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset,'minute')` is also computed four times; compute each shifted value once. `timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange` (packages/types/schedule.d.ts:5), and `.tz(undefined)` here falls back to the server's local zone. That is harmless today because `getSchedule` always sets it, but it would silently use the wrong zone for any other caller.

findings.title: New test only covers one invitee offset and none of the new availability checks
findings.body: The added case checks a single invitee zone (+6:00) against an organizer in +5:30. It does not cover an invitee whose offset puts the override across midnight (see lib/slots.ts finding), a host with two blocks on one day, or a slot that runs past the end of a working block. The last two are the paths where the new `checkIfIsAvailable` working-hours logic is wrong. Round-robin and fixed-host date-override scenarios named in the PR description are also untested.

contracts.action: New date-override and working-hours availability checks inside checkIfIsAvailable, called for fixed hosts, loose hosts and selected-slot busy checks
contracts.equivalent_path: getSlots in packages/lib/slots.ts already applies working hours and date overrides when generating candidate slots (lines 163-246); checkIfIsAvailable previously only checked busy times and seats.
contracts.before_after: Fixed and loose host call sites spread `...schedule`, so `workingHours` and `dateOverrides` now reach the check (lines 488-493, 513-518). The selectedSlots call site (581-586) passes neither, so both default to [] and only busy times are checked there, as before.
contracts.visible_effect: Slots are removed from the result returned by getSchedule and shown to the booker. A host with multiple availability blocks in one day loses all slots on that day.
contracts.failure_mode: The check does not throw. It silently returns false, so slots disappear with no error.

contracts.action: Shift date-override minutes by invitee-minus-organizer UTC offset when building slots
contracts.equivalent_path: Working hours are localised to the invitee by getWorkingHours with a negated invitee utcOffset and clamped to 0-1439 (lines 170-176); overrides previously used raw UTC minutes.
contracts.before_after: Overrides are now shifted by the offset but not clamped or split across days, unlike working hours.
contracts.visible_effect: Override slots in the invitee's zone match the organizer's intended local hours for small offsets. For large offsets that cross midnight they are dropped or misplaced.
contracts.failure_mode: When end < start after wrapping, buildSlots skips the entry (line 68) and the day's regular hours were already removed, so the day silently has no slots.

summary: The date-override timezone shift in lib/slots.ts is correct for small offsets. However, the new working-hours check in checkIfIsAvailable breaks any host with more than one availability block on a day: `find` fails the slot if it is outside any block, so all slots vanish. The `end` variable duplicates `start`, so slot end times are never checked. The shifted overrides can also wrap past midnight and silently drop a day's slots. The new test covers one offset only, and none of these cases.
